extracted.intended_audience: readers of Popular Science Monthly; general scientifically-interested readers, book buyers, and reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and evaluative remarks used by a periodical reviewer when assessing scientific, popular-science, travel, and scholarly books for a general readership; emphasizes accuracy, accessibility, scope, illustrations, and practical impact. Applicable to reviewing or producing books aimed at educating or influencing the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose: diagnosis and exhortation
rubrics_metrics.description: Book's object should point out common and fruitful sources of debilities and infirmities and arouse readers to more earnest, hearty, and determined effort at amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works intended to reform or improve public habits are judged by how clearly they identify causes and how effectively they motivate corrective action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factual accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: If the objection implies that facts are distorted or truth overstrained, it should have a real basis; factual distortion is not excused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even persuasive or rhetorically strong works must not sacrifice accuracy; accusations of exaggeration should be distinguished from outright misstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate rhetorical force
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of superlatives and strong speech is excusable when writing for the people with the hope of mending things; non-committal under-statements are not best suited to that purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bold, vivid language is acceptable—indeed desirable—when the aim is to arouse indignation and provoke action, provided facts remain sound.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and emotional resonance
rubrics_metrics.description: A good popular work should be such that 'everybody can understand it, and, what is more, feel it,' and be likely 'to read and re-read it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate readability for general audiences and the capacity to move readers emotionally as part of a book's value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical utility and distributability
rubrics_metrics.description: A salutary book should be widely distributed: those able should buy it wholesale and give it to those less able to obtain it; it 'will be a boon to benighted multitudes.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the work has practical implications and can be readily disseminated to have social impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensiveness of topical coverage (travel/narrative works)
rubrics_metrics.description: A successful voyage account gives history, geographical descriptions, natural history, geology, and delineations of the people—'touching nearly all the subjects of interest appertaining to them.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review travel/scientific narratives for breadth across relevant subject-matters and the inclusion of contextual material (history, natural history, peoples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual/historical framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Including the history of previous voyages and their narratives adds variety and supplies content (dangers, misfortunes) readers may expect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good accounts situate their own narrative within prior work to enrich the reader's understanding and interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descriptive richness and exactness
rubrics_metrics.description: Geographical and natural descriptions should be full, interesting, and render previously vague notions distinct and exact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the vividness and precision of landscape, sea, and seasonal phenomena descriptions; they should inform and correct vague preconceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respectful ethnographic depiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Accounts of indigenous tribes (e.g., Samoyeds, Chuckchees) should be 'in the kindliest of feeling and with delicate humor' and valuable as anthropological studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate tone and sensitivity in describing peoples: avoid condescension; prioritize humane, informative portrayals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic/geographical analysis of practical value
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessments of regions should estimate productive capacity and possible value to the world's economy, even if surprising preconceived notions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Travel/scientific works that discuss commercial feasibility or resource potential should be judged on the rigor and plausibility of such estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and significance of accomplishment
rubrics_metrics.description: The first full account of an enterprise (e.g., forcing a northeast passage / first circumnavigation of Europe and Asia) has special interest and value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give weight to works that document novel achievements or firsts in exploration or science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authoritative competence
rubrics_metrics.description: Works should be authored or edited by competent authorities (e.g., 'Mr. Davids... one of the most competent living authorities on the subject').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the author's credentials and standing in the field when judging scholarly or historical works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate scope selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Choosing the proper geographical or topical focus (e.g., selecting India to elucidate Buddhism's fundamentals) is a mark of sound judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the chosen scope best serves the book's explanatory aims and primary sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarly thoroughness and use of primary texts
rubrics_metrics.description: Lectures consider principal books (e.g., Pali Pitakas), doctrines, rules, and later forms; such thorough treatment merits 'profound and respectful study.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge works for the depth of engagement with foundational texts and doctrinal detail appropriate to the subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and affordability of scientific publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Setting the example of publishing scientific books in cheap editions is commended (translator aims to publish in cheap editions as abroad).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the price and availability of scientific works as part of their public value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and provenance of illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Plates and illustrations drawn by the author (e.g., figures by Dr. Cohn) and the excellence of illustrations are important merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the accuracy, clarity, and source of illustrations; original author-drawn plates are particularly valuable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and coherence of central thesis
rubrics_metrics.description: Works that present a clear summation of central points (e.g., 'man is the animal that has learned to think of himself...') are valued for coherence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether an author's main theses are clearly stated and developed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical, case-based relevance (medical proceedings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Medical papers based upon material drawn chiefly from cases in the practice of their authors and treating appropriate subjects in medical and surgical treatment are of general interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In clinical fields, prioritize case-based evidence and practical applicability to practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of illustrations where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrations are included 'where the matter calls for them' (e.g., medical papers), indicating the need for visual support when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that works provide diagrams, plates, or figures when the subject matter benefits from them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balancing vividness with scientific dignity and accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Present facts to the non-scientific public 'in such a style that it will read of them with the interest with which it follows the development of a romance, without detracting from the dignity and accuracy of scientific statement' and 'without falling into exaggeration and sensationalism.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Popular-science writing should captivate readers while maintaining rigor and avoiding sensationalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pedagogical aim to inspire further study
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should aim to 'inspire and extend a taste for natural science' and present 'not a learned treatise, but a simple elementary study' conceived to induce readers to seek more extensive works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether a work successfully serves as an entry point that motivates further, deeper study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate audience-level targeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Some works should be suitable for both child and student equally; readability for varied audience levels is a merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether tone, exposition, and examples match the intended readership (children, general readers, students).

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical correctness in instruction (voice-production)
rubrics_metrics.description: Voice-culture foundations: breathing should be full and easy, performed by diaphragm muscles, not clavicle or ribs; technique consists in learning when organs act properly and how to make them act so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructional texts should base technique on correct physiological principles and provide actionable guidance/exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical specificity and exemplars
rubrics_metrics.description: Particular technical points (e.g., articulate action of the glottis, fractional tones) should be illustrated by high-level exemplars (Nilsson, Santley, Madame Mara).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include concrete technical descriptions and exemplary demonstrations or historical cases to substantiate claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative perspective and engagement with contemporary research
rubrics_metrics.description: Setting forth what has been done in Europe and America on a topic (e.g., trance, muscle-reading) allows comparison and contextual understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works that synthesize cross-regional research and offer comparative insights are valuable for assessing the state of a field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone: entertaining yet instructive
rubrics_metrics.description: Essays intended for the general reader should be pleasant, descriptive, scientific, and philosophic—'intended to suit the general reader'—and 'provocative of thought.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether a book balances entertainment with informative content to stimulate reader interest and reflection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematic, philosophical organization (textbooks)
rubrics_metrics.description: A chemical philosophy text aims to present the great body of chemical truths in a 'closely correlated and thoroughly systematized form' to give breadth and dignity to the student's knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Textbooks should organize material deductively/systematically and aim to relate facts into an integrated whole rather than as isolated items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role as supplement to practical teaching
rubrics_metrics.description: Such works are 'not intended to take the place of laboratory teaching, but solely to supplement it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify and judge a book according to its declared role: whether it complements practical training or is designed for independent instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Currency and incorporation of recent progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Revisions that thoroughly embody the results of the last ten years of progress and bring forward many features for the first time are meritorious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether revised editions adequately incorporate recent developments and new knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological reliability and practicality (analytical methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analytical methods for milk claim superiority over previous methods in accuracy, simplicity, and in cheapness and economy of time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate laboratory methods for precision, simplicity, cost-effectiveness, and time economy; practical applicability matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal to improve nomenclature and intelligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A revision of anatomical nomenclature to abbreviate, simplify, and make it more intelligible is proposed as a merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess contributions that reduce terminological confusion and enhance clarity for readers and practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of institutional bibliographies
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists intended to include books, pamphlets, reports, and contributions printed during a time span, by institute officers, students, alumni, etc., should be comprehensive and cover a variety of subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge bibliographic compilations on inclusiveness, scope, and accuracy of entries.
